Jordan / Priya / Ellen —

Thanks for the quick reply and for adding Ellen. Based on internal experience with similar pilots I sketched three timeline lanes in an updated attachment (MAP_timeline_options_v2.xlsx). Below is a short summary so stakeholders can choose quickly.

Option A — Aggressive (4–6 weeks)
- Preconditions: procurement and security review prioritized, DPA signed in parallel, pilot data access provisioned within 5 business days.
- Pros: fastest time-to-value; keeps exec momentum high.
- Cons: requires dedicated review owners and near-immediate signoffs.

Option B — Standard (8–10 weeks) — recommended
- Preconditions: typical legal and procurement cycles, security packet reviewed within 2 weeks, engineering slot reserved for integration testing.
- Pros: balanced risk and velocity; realistic for mid-market customers.
- Cons: slightly longer ramp for measurement and iteration.

Option C — Conservative (12+ weeks)
- Preconditions: procurement on its normal cadence, security review after pilot results, or if internal QA scheduling is constrained.
- Pros: low process friction.
- Cons: slows business impact and may complicate resource scheduling.

Please:
- Confirm which option you prefer (A / B / C).
- Confirm the point people for Milestone 1–4 (I put suggested names in the sheet).
- Confirm any additional dependencies (e.g., vendor risk assessment owner, legal intake ticket number).

Sean / Monica — tagging you both to keep this thread in the loop for delivery and any pricing contingencies depending on the chosen lane. If Jordan confirms Option A we may need to request a fast-track procurement review and a short credit hold.

Next steps I can take immediately: create a shared Google Sheet, schedule a 30-minute align for stakeholders, or prepare a one-page SOW draft conditioned on Option selection.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
